diagnoses.description: Total selection failed due to OCR digit-flip outlier on a later, high-priority keyword line (e.g., “Total Amt Rounded”), overriding multiple internal anchors (Subtotal/Payment/Total incl) that agree on a different value. This is a classic case where keyword-priority or “last TOTAL wins” must be subordinated to receipt-internal consistency.
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 074.jpg amount_correct=false while date_correct=true; prediction total_amount="702.00". Visual inspection of 074.jpg shows multiple summary anchors around 102.00 (Subtotal, Total incl. of GST, Total Amt Rounded, Payment). The packet’s trace shows OCR variants can produce both 702.00 and 102.00, indicating a 1→7 digit flip on one line. Selection logic must reject candidates contradicting multiple anchors even if they appear on a higher-priority keyword line.

diagnoses.description: Rounding precedence failure: the extractor selected the pre-rounding inclusive total instead of the final payable TOTAL after a rounding adjustment, causing an exact-match miss (often by 0.01).
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 077.jpg amount_correct=false while date_correct=true; prediction total_amount="23.26". Visual inspection of 077.jpg shows “Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26”, then “Rounding Adj: -0.01”, then bold “TOTAL: 23.25”. This indicates the pipeline did not enforce the hard precedence rule: if a rounding adjustment exists and a later TOTAL exists, always take the later TOTAL.

diagnoses.description: Coupled extraction + schema failure: total_amount was emitted as an empty string instead of null, violating the task schema. This receipt also contains an “Amount” column header that can trigger split-line fallback to an item amount unless explicitly excluded; OCR may corrupt both the GRAND TOTAL keyword and the decimal separator (e.g., 92:80).
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 078.jpg amount_correct=false; prediction total_amount="" (empty string). Visual inspection of 078.jpg shows a table header “Description Qty Price Amount” and summary lines “Total: 92.80” / “Grand Total: 92.80” plus payment lines “Cash Received: 100.00”, “Change: 7.20”. The packet’s trace shows header-triggered split-line fallback and punctuation corruption (92:80) and keyword corruption (GrandTota./GrandTotal.), requiring explicit header exclusion, tight fallback gating, decimal normalization, and a final schema guard (empty/whitespace → null).

diagnoses.description: Date disambiguation failure: the run selected a secondary date-like token (or an OCR-corrupted label line such as DATE→DATA) instead of the primary header Date field on a dense invoice with multiple date-like strings.
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 034.jpg date_correct=false while amount_correct=true; prediction date=2018-08-09. Visual inspection of 034.jpg shows a clear header block with a labeled Date field near the top (dd/mm/yyyy) and other header-adjacent date/time-like strings. Prior history indicates OCR label corruption (DATE→DATA) can create competing labeled candidates, making naive first-match or weak ranking brittle.

quality_impact.rationale: The current candidate image-ocr skill already encodes the minimal, transferable fixes implied by the historical failures: header/label-tolerant date ranking (034), anchor-driven outlier rejection and conditional upscale OCR passes (074), hard rounding precedence (077), explicit exclusion of AMOUNT column headers + tight split-line fallback + tolerant GRAND TOTAL matching + decimal-separator normalization + empty-string→null guard (078). Additional edits would be largely redundant; remaining risk is downstream implementation adherence rather than missing skill guidance.

trigger_precision.rationale: Existing guidance is narrowly scoped to receipt OCR and triggers only under specific conditions (e.g., split-line fallback only when keyword line has no digits and is not a header; anchor override only when multiple anchors agree; optional upscaling only as fallback). No additional broadening is needed.

instruction_compliance.rationale: Diagnoses rely only on permitted evidence (field-level correctness feedback, predictions, and provided images/OCR snippets). No oracle values are referenced. No tool execution is requested. No unnecessary skill files are modified.

solution_path_coverage.rationale: Covers all observed failure classes in the run: wrong date among multiple candidates (034), wrong total due to OCR digit flip/outlier (074), wrong total due to rounding precedence (077), and schema/normalization + header-triggered fallback issues (078).

skillaxe_evaluation.overall_rationale: The packet’s evidence indicates the original run’s misses were dominated by receipt-specific selection/normalization under OCR noise, not missing OCR capability. The current candidate image-ocr skill already contains the necessary heuristics; the most effective next step is ensuring implementations actually apply them (anchor-consistency override, rounding precedence, header-line exclusion, and final schema guard).

iteration_summary: Diagnosed the four incorrect fields (034 date; 074/077/078 totals) using allowed feedback and the provided images/OCR snippets. No SKILL.md updates proposed because the current candidate image-ocr skill already addresses these failure modes; remaining risk is implementation adherence rather than missing guidance.
